theory.intro: A transformation moves a shape to a new position. The three transformations are translation (slide), reflection (flip) and rotation (turn). The shape keeps its size and shape.
steps: Compare the image with the original.
If it has slid → translation; flipped → reflection; turned → rotation.
Describe the amount: how far/direction for a slide, the mirror line for a flip, the angle for a turn.

foundation.solution_text:
The shape has slid right and up without turning or flipping.
Translation
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\draw (0,0)--(1.4,0)--(1.4,0.6)--(0.6,0.6)--(0.6,1.8)--(0,1.8)--cycle;\draw (3,1)--(4.4,1)--(4.4,1.6)--(3.6,1.6)--(3.6,2.8)--(3,2.8)--cycle;\draw[->,dashed] (1.1,1.1)--(3.2,1.8);\node[below] at (0.7,0) {$A$};\node[below] at (3.7,1) {$B$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

The shapes are mirror images on opposite sides of the dashed line.
Reflection
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\draw (-2.3,0)--(-0.7,0)--(-0.7,1.5)--(-1.3,0.8)--(-2.3,0.8)--cycle;\draw[thick,dashed] (0,-0.4)--(0,2) node[above] {mirror line};\draw (2.3,0)--(0.7,0)--(0.7,1.5)--(1.3,0.8)--(2.3,0.8)--cycle;\draw[<->,dashed] (-1.3,0.8)--(1.3,0.8);
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

The shape has turned about point $O$ without being flipped.
Rotation
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw (0.5,0.5)--(2.2,0.5)--(0.5,1.4)--cycle;\draw (-0.5,0.5)--(-0.5,2.2)--(-1.4,0.5)--cycle;\draw[dashed] (O)--(0.5,0.5);\draw[dashed] (O)--(-0.5,0.5);\fill (O) circle (1.5pt);\node[below] at (O) {centre $O$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

foundation.question_text:
A tile slides $4$ squares right and $2$ squares down without turning.
Describe the transformation.
foundation.solution_text: Translation $4$ squares right and $2$ squares down

foundation.question_text:
A flag is flipped across a vertical mirror line.
Describe the transformation.
foundation.solution_text: Reflection in the vertical mirror line

foundation.question_text:
An arrow turns one quarter-turn clockwise about point $C$.
Describe the transformation using an angle.
foundation.solution_text:
A quarter-turn is $90^{\circ}$.
Rotation $90^{\circ}$ clockwise about $C$

development.solution_text:
A matching vertex moves $4$ squares right and $2$ squares down, and the orientation stays the same.
Translation $4$ squares right and $2$ squares down
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (0,0) grid (6,4);\draw (0.3,2.3)--(1.7,2.3)--(1.7,3.3)--(0.8,2.8)--cycle;\draw (4.3,0.3)--(5.7,0.3)--(5.7,1.3)--(4.8,0.8)--cycle;\draw[->,thick,dashed] (0.3,2.3)--(4.3,0.3);
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

Corresponding points are the same distance from the vertical dashed line on opposite sides.
Reflection in the vertical dashed line
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\draw[gray!30,very thin] (-3,-1) grid (3,3);\draw[thick,dashed] (0,-1.4)--(0,3.4);\draw[fill=gray!25] (-2.7,-0.7)--(-0.7,-0.7)--(-2.7,2.3)--cycle;\draw (2.7,-0.7)--(0.7,-0.7)--(2.7,2.3)--cycle;\draw[<->,dashed] (-2.7,2.3)--(2.7,2.3);
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

The direction changes from right to down, which is a quarter-turn clockwise about $O$.
Rotation $90^{\circ}$ clockwise about $O$
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\coordinate (O) at (0,0);\draw[->] (0.6,0.5)--(2.4,0.5);\draw[->] (0.5,-0.6)--(0.5,-2.4);\draw[dashed] (O)--(0.6,0.5);\draw[dashed] (O)--(0.5,-0.6);\fill (O) circle (1.5pt);\node[above left] at (O) {$O$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

Each point moves to the opposite side of $C$, and the arrow reverses direction.
Rotation $180^{\circ}$ about $C$
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\coordinate (C) at (0,0);\draw[->] (-0.6,0.7)--(-2.3,1.5);\draw[->] (0.6,-0.7)--(2.3,-1.5);\draw[dashed] (-0.6,0.7)--(0.6,-0.7);\fill (C) circle (1.5pt);\node[above right] at (C) {centre $C$};
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]

development.question_text:
Kai says that moving a shape from the left of a line to the right must be a reflection.
Explain why that is not enough information.
development.solution_text:
A translation can also move a shape from left to right.
It is a reflection only if the image is flipped and corresponding points are equally far from the mirror line.

development.question_text:
A shape and its image have the same orientation, and every point has moved the same distance in the same direction.
Identify the transformation and explain why it cannot be a rotation.
development.solution_text:
Every point making the same straight move describes a translation.
A rotation turns points around a centre, so their directions of movement are not all the same.

mastery.question_text:
A shape turns from pointing north-east to pointing south-west about point $K$.
Describe the smallest rotation that does this.
mastery.solution_text:
North-east and south-west are opposite directions, so the turn is a half-turn.
Rotation $180^{\circ}$ about $K$

Mia is not correct. All three transformations preserve size.
Here the image is back-to-front across the dashed line, so it is a reflection.

mastery.question_text:
A shape moves to a new position and its orientation changes.
Give two possible kinds of transformation, and state one extra observation that would distinguish them.
mastery.solution_text:
The move could be a reflection or a rotation.
A reflection produces a mirror image across a line; a rotation turns the shape about a fixed point.
